ruleName: Puddles and other abnormal course conditions
group: Puddles and other abnormal course conditions
title: Taking relief from a puddle or abnormal course condition
question: Your ball is on the putting green and there is a puddle between your ball and the hole, affecting your line of play. What do the rules say you are allowed to do?

choices.text: Place the ball at the nearest spot where the puddle does not affect your line, no closer to the hole, with no penalty.
Try to avoid the puddle and play your ball as it lies.
Place your ball closer to the hole to find a dry line.
Take a penalty stroke and drop your ball anywhere on the green.

explanation: You are allowed to place your ball at the nearest point where the puddle does not interfere, not nearer the hole, with no penalty.
imagePrompt: A teenage golfer placing the ball on the putting green to the nearest point of relief from a puddle affecting the line to the hole.
imageAlt: Teen golfer on the green placing ball to avoid puddle, not nearer the hole.

issues: The golfer appears to be right-handed instead of left-handed.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Ensure the teenage boy is clearly left-handed in his action when dropping the ball; the putter should be held in the right hand, with the ball being dropped from the left hand.
